name: profile_ctx2k
description: Profiling workload for the v1.0.162 Nsight pass. Single prompt of ~1900 tokens of representative English so ctx≈2k by the end of decode. Deterministic (temperature=0, seed=42). 200 decode tokens — enough warm steps for nsys/ncu to capture a stable averaged kernel profile.

prompts.text:
Below is a sequence of paragraphs describing the architecture, design choices, and runtime behaviour of a hypothetical inference engine.  The engine targets consumer-grade GPUs and emphasises mixture-of-experts routing with hybridised quantisation.  Read it carefully and then continue from where it stops.

The engine has 48 transformer blocks. Each block runs Grouped-Query Attention with 32 query heads, 4 KV heads, and a head dimension of 128.  Rotary positional embeddings use a theta of 10 million.  Pre-attention and post-attention normalisations are RMSNorm.  The MoE FFN replaces a dense feed-forward network and routes each token through 8 of 128 experts.  Each expert is a SwiGLU with hidden dimension 768 and projection dimension 2048.

Weight storage is hybrid.  Edge layers — typically the first 4 and last 4 transformer blocks — keep their MoE FFN weights as Q4_K because numerical fidelity at the boundary dominates downstream quality.  Interior layers store their MoE FFN weights as a custom packed-ternary format: each group of 64 weights becomes 18 bytes, a 2-byte FP16 scale followed by 16 bytes of 2-bit codes.  The codes represent ternary states: 0 means zero weight, 1 means positive scale, 2 means negative scale.  A separate code 3 is reserved and never emitted.

A recently shipped optional compression layer wraps the ternary stream in a Huffman code derived from the measured symbol distribution.  Code 0 maps to one bit, codes 1 and 2 each map to two bits, code 3 is unused.  The on-disk ternary payload shrinks by about 18.7 per cent on Qwen-shape models with bit-identical decoding.  At load time the engine either decodes the Huffman payload back to the original packed-ternary layout host-side or, when CUDA is enabled, streams the encoded bytes to device memory and decodes them with a per-row CUDA kernel.

Materialising an expert into VRAM follows a layered policy.  The fastest path is a VramPool slot allocator: a single contiguous slot per expert holds gate, up, and down weights end-to-end, with each sub-tensor 256-byte aligned for coalesced loads.  Each model's expert size is uniform so a single slot size always fits.  If the pool is full the engine falls back to a per-expert cudaMalloc, then to host-pinned RAM, then to memory-mapped file pages.

A persistent decode workspace caches the H2D'd encoded payload and row offsets in device memory keyed by host blob pointer.  Once a bulk MoE FFN tensor has been streamed up to VRAM, all eight routed experts of that layer share the same device copy.  The cache eliminates redundant memory copies and keeps the per-step transfer cost flat in the number of unique bulk tensors touched, not the number of experts.

A companion model variant uses Gated DeltaNet attention layers in place of standard attention every third block.  The interleave reduces compute on long contexts at the cost of more state to carry through the residual stream.  These layers have higher fixed per-token overhead and benefit from larger batch sizes, but at batch one they pay a memory-bandwidth penalty in exchange for the long-context win.

The scheduler runs an entropy controller that maps the running attention entropy estimate H to a policy.  When H is below a low threshold the regime is Stable: the recommended batch grows and the speculative-decode depth recommendation rises to six.  When H is above a high threshold the regime is Stress: batch shrinks, speculation is suppressed, and the predictor falls back to deterministic argmax.

Speculative decoding combines a primary drafter and a verifier.  The drafter is Prompt-Lookup Decoding, a zero-training scheme that walks a rolling buffer of recently observed tokens for matches against the last few-token needle, then proposes whatever followed the prior occurrence.  The verifier runs a batched multi-position forward over shared KV cache to produce target log-probabilities for each draft token, then accepts a prefix using rejection sampling against the draft log-probs.

The runtime exposes a small set of opt-in tunables.  ECSIE_PREWARM_HNTT controls whether the per-bulk decode cache is filled during model load: useful on GPUs with VRAM headroom, harmful on memory-tight cards where pre-warm pushes activations out of cache.  ECSIE_SPEC enables the speculative decode pipeline.  ECSIE_FUSED_MULTI_TERNARY toggles the fused multi-expert ternary FFN dispatch path.

Determinism is preserved across the optional optimisation paths: a byte-equivalence test compares generated token IDs against a reference run with all paths disabled.  Any regression that breaks bit-exact equivalence is blocked from landing.  Quantisation-induced numerical drift is bounded by L2 reconstruction error checks at conversion time, with activation-aware grid alignment driven by the SqueezeLLM unsupervised proxy: per-input-column L2-norm squared of the source weights.

The disk format is a thin extension of GGUF.  Tensor type identifiers 100 and 101 are reserved for the packed-ternary and Huffman-encoded variants respectively, and the engine's loader dispatches on the on-disk type while presenting the decoded payload to downstream kernels as ordinary type-100 packed ternary.  The format is forward-compatible: a writer can emit type 101 and a reader without Huffman support falls back to a clear error message rather than producing silent garbage.

Profiling work focuses on locating the true bottleneck during steady-state decode.  Hypotheses to verify include the PCIe transfer ceiling, the MoE GEMM kernels' compute versus memory bound status, the cost of kernel launch overhead at small batch sizes, and any accidental synchronisations introduced by the cache or workspace code.  The answer matters because every later optimisation should be aimed at a confirmed bottleneck, not an assumed one.  Now continue the analysis below.
